notes: Tethering rebuilt: press tether to see snap points in reach, step through them, press again to attach. Cleaner glowing cable with a clamp.
Controller: RB is now the tether (tap to attach or release, hold to reel) and a click of the left stick toggles boost.
New sonar ping: a soft wave that runs along the seabed, glints on chests, surveys, stations, recoveries and animals, and a note of what it found.
Falling stars now leave rare glowing star chests. A star gives a direction and a search circle on the chart, and the chest hums when you are close.
Star chests pay 60 / 120 / 250 sand dollars and are rarer.
Missions: notebook-style notices and details page, details open with the interact key, and jobs beyond your pressure rating are locked.
Shop on a controller: moving over an item previews it, A fits it, X / Y change category, A fits upgrades.
Chart: left stick moves the view, softer view cone, smooth island edges, tidier header and buttons.
Chest, station and scenic stop prompts use the same dial card as recording a survey.
Unlocks are spread across the whole expedition instead of the first few surveys.

Fixed: offshore fish that were blank and frozen, sonar not firing while moving on a controller, kelp growing through station platforms, the Fishbowl's floor poking through its dome, overlapping prompts near stations.
Steering is inverted while reversing, like a car.
Postcard mode removed. US English spelling throughout.

Fixed: offshore fish that were blank and frozen, sonar not firing while moving on a controller, kelp growing through station platforms, the Fishbowl's floor poking through its dome, overlapping prompts near stations.
Steering is inverted while reversing, like a car.
Postcard mode removed. US English spelling throughout.
The caves now look like natural rock outcrops that match the stone around them, instead of long tubes.
Four new dead-end caves to find in the Lantern Archipelago, each with one mouth and glowing fans at the back.
New sound above the water: gulls in fair weather, wind, rain and thunder in storms, and waves washing on the island shores.
The blue whale now has a call, and the water sounds are a little louder.
Five new calm piano tracks on the radio.
New guided first dive: June talks you through the controls one at a time, a first survey, a first animal photo and the trip home to the workshop. Hold Backspace to skip it.
June has a new portrait and an animated speech bubble, with a soft talking sound as her words appear.
The briefing is shorter: the control cards moved into the first dive.
Surveys, landmarks, unlocks, chests and new subs now arrive as small notebook slips on the left, each with its own icon. The large centre text is gone.
The song and artist now show under the map name while the radio is on.
Subs float at the right height on the surface.
The whale bones are rebuilt as a proper skeleton and renamed "The leviathan arch".
The up/down speed readout under the depth gauge is removed.
New opening: the R.V. Lost Cause, a briefing from June and the sub launch, in daylight. Enter or A moves on, Esc skips.
Finish everything in the Lantern Archipelago, then board the ship to sail to Frostglass Shelf. The old portal is gone.
Clean title cards for discoveries, landmarks and unlocks.
Distant land on the horizon is now clean layered silhouettes.
Stations are named: Lantern station is home, the others are "<name> station".
Sub models detailed: Longfin, Needle, Bell, Twinfin. Terrapin rebuilt as a domed sub. Hermit slimmed down. Fishbowl hatch fixed.
New cabin interiors on eight subs: proper pilot seats, control yokes, displays, gauges and pedals.
Bow arms, the bumper and the halo lights no longer run through each other; the bumper opens into two rails when an arm is fitted.
